newsitem.title: TUNISIA: Gaddafi defends Erbakan on trip to Libya.
newsitem.headline: Gaddafi defends Erbakan on trip to Libya.

text.p: Libyan leader Muammar Gaddafi on Tuesday defended Turkish Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan, who was attacked at home for visiting a country whose leader professed support for a Kurdish state.
The official Libyan news agency JANA also quoted Gaddafi as saying that Turkish Foreign Minister Tansu Ciller, who went to Libya in 1994 when she was prime minister, shared his feelings on the Kurds.
"Ciller...likes Kurds as I do, as she told me that during her last visit to Libya, but she complains over the PKK," Gaddafi said.

The PKK, which stands for the Kurdistan Workers Party, is fighting for self-rule in southeast Turkey, a 12-year-old battle in which more than 20,000 people have died. Turkish law bans statements in support of a Kurdish state.

The opposition and the Turkish media have slammed Erbakan for the visit during which Gaddafi strongly criticised NATO-member Turkey's treatment of its minority Kurdish population and its ties to the West.
Turkey has already said it would recall its ambassador from Tripoli because of Gaddafi's statements.
In the comments carried by JANA, Gaddafi said Libya would pay its debts to Turkish contractors -- one of the things Erbakan had hoped to resolve in his trip.
